messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT - geo-dns anomaly detected for eu cluster (model-serving.api.redwood.com). elevated resolution failures and increased latency. paging on-call.

maria: acked. I'm on it — pulling up Route53/Cloudflare metrics now.

jon-oncall: on-call here, acknowledging. what's the customer impact? 5xxs or timeouts?

maria: primarily NXDOMAIN and intermittent timeouts for eu endpoints. some customers report requests falling back to other regions. started ~09:12 UTC.

kevin: looking at Cloudflare resolver logs — spike in SERVFAILs from a subset of edge resolvers.

sasha: running quick dig from eu-west-1: 
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 model-serving.api.redwood.com A
; inconsistent answers, sometimes blank
```

maria: Route53 healthcheck for eu origin shows intermittent 502s. TTL is 60s but propagation jitter is giving split answers between primary and fallback.

ops-bot: created mitigation task mitigate/dns-eu-propagation-4981234567 and assigned to network.

jon-oncall: tentative plan: 
1) failover Route53 record to secondary origin (eu-fallback)
2) reduce TTL temporarily to 30s
3) pause Cloudflare proxy for affected records to reduce resolver cache churn
4) drain eu AZ nodes if origin instability persists

kevin: executing Route53 failover now -> switching to eu-fallback-target. applying lower TTL.

maria: Route53 change applied. console shows failover active and TTL 30s. propagating.

sasha: re-checking from public resolvers: 
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 model-serving.api.redwood.com
3.7.2.1
```

maria: traffic is shifting to fallback; error rate dropping from ~15% to ~3%.

oliver: opened Cloudflare ticket (CF-49812) and posted support link: https://support.cloudflare.com/incident/CF-49812 (internal ref).

emily-support: drafting customer advisory: "We experienced DNS resolution instability in EU between 09:12-09:26 UTC. Traffic was routed to a fallback origin; applications may have seen transient errors. We're monitoring and will follow up with a post-incident summary."

maria: suspected root cause: upstream resolver IP flapping + stale cache entries between CF and Route53 leading to split-horizon responses.

kevin: recommended to keep Route53 failover in place for 30m, increase healthcheck sensitivity, and monitor resolver error rates.

sasha: submitting short resolver log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T09:13:05Z resolver-lookup id=abc123 src=1.2.3.4 outcome=SERVFAIL
2026-03-15T09:13:07Z resolver-lookup id=abc124 src=5.6.7.8 outcome=NOERROR ans=A 3.7.2.1
```

maria: handing off watch to night on-call @jon-night for monitoring and postmortem writeup. include Cloudflare ticket and Route53 change details.

jon-night: taking the watch. I'll keep an eye on alerts and prepare the incident timeline and action items.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE - severity changed to degraded (recovered) — error rate stabilized ~1.2% during stabilization window.

jon-night: will keep the failover for 30m then evaluate re-targeting to primary after confirming low error rates. closing Slack thread for now; will reopen if anomaly returns. :thumbsup:
